title: Congruence Class
content: **CongruenceClass a n**: The set of integers congruent to $a \pmod{n}$, defined as $\{x \in \mathbb{Z} : x \bmod n = a \bmod n\}$. Each congruence class has natural density $1/n$ — asymptotically, exactly $1/n$ of all integers belong to it. For example, $\text{CongruenceClass}(1, 3) = \{\ldots, -2, 1, 4, 7, 10, \ldots\}$.

title: Covering System Structure
content: **CoveringSystem**: A structure containing `classes : Finset (ℤ × ℕ)` — pairs $(a_i, n_i)$ representing congruence classes — together with proofs of `nonempty` (at least one class), `positive_moduli` ($\forall p \in \text{classes}, p.2 > 0$), and `covers` ($\forall x, \exists p \in \text{classes}, x \bmod p.2 = p.1 \bmod p.2$). This models a finite collection of congruence classes that covers all of $\mathbb{Z}$.
mathContext: $\text{CoveringSystem} = (\{(a_i, n_i)\}, n_i > 0, \forall x\, \exists i : x \equiv a_i \pmod{n_i})$

title: Distinct Moduli and Exact Covering
content:
**hasDistinctModuli C**: All moduli in the system are different — if $p.2 = q.2$ for $p, q \in C.\text{classes}$ then $p = q$. This is modulus-injectivity.

**isExact C**: Every integer satisfies exactly one congruence, formalized using $\exists!$ (exists unique): $\forall x, \exists! p, p \in C.\text{classes} \wedge x \bmod p.2 = p.1 \bmod p.2$. This is the partition property — the congruence classes are pairwise disjoint and jointly exhaustive.
mathContext: $\text{hasDistinctModuli}(C) \iff \text{moduli injective}; \quad \text{isExact}(C) \iff \forall x, \exists! p \in C : x \equiv p.1 \pmod{p.2}$

title: Density and Density Sum
content:
**density n**: The natural density of a congruence class $a \pmod{n}$, defined as $1/n$ in $\mathbb{Q}$.

**densitySum C**: The sum $\sum_{p \in C.\text{classes}} 1/p.2$, computed via `Finset.sum`. For an exact covering (partition of $\mathbb{Z}$), this sum must equal 1 since the classes are disjoint and cover everything. For Erdős's example $\{2, 3, 4, 6, 12\}$: $1/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + 1/6 + 1/12 = 15/12 > 1$, confirming overlaps.

title: Density Sum Equals 1 for Exact Coverings
content: **exact_density_sum**: Axiomatizes that for an exact covering system $C$, $\text{densitySum}(C) = 1$. If the congruence classes partition $\mathbb{Z}$, their natural densities must sum to 1 (the density of $\mathbb{Z}$ itself). This is the starting point for both proofs of impossibility: combined with LCM constraints, $\sum 1/n_i = 1$ with distinct $n_i$ leads to contradictions.

title: Mirsky-Newman / Davenport-Rado Impossibility
content: **no_exact_covering_system**: Axiomatizes the central result: $\neg\exists C : \text{CoveringSystem}, \text{hasDistinctModuli}(C) \wedge \text{isExact}(C)$. No finite collection of congruence classes with all different moduli can partition $\mathbb{Z}$. Proved independently by Mirsky-Newman (generating functions) and Davenport-Rado (LCM divisibility).

title: Distinct Moduli Implies Not Exact
content: **distinct_moduli_not_exact**: *Proved*: $\forall C, \text{hasDistinctModuli}(C) \to \neg\text{isExact}(C)$. The universal contrapositive of `no_exact_covering_system`. The proof constructs the existential witness from the hypotheses and applies the axiomatized impossibility: `⟨C, hD, hE⟩` witnesses the negated statement, then `no_exact_covering_system` gives the contradiction.

title: Mirsky-Newman Generating Function Argument
content: **mirsky_newman_argument**: Axiomatizes the generating function approach. For an exact covering with distinct moduli, the formal power series $f(x) = \sum_i x^{a_i}/(1 - x^{n_i})$ must equal $1/(1-x)$. The axiom states that under these hypotheses, $\text{densitySum}(C) = 1$ — a consequence but not the full strength of the analytic argument, which shows the identity is impossible at roots of unity.

title: Davenport-Rado LCM Argument
content: **davenport_rado_argument**: Axiomatizes the LCM divisibility approach. For an exact covering with distinct moduli $n_1 < \cdots < n_k$, the largest modulus $n_k$ must divide $\text{lcm}(n_1, \ldots, n_{k-1})$, computed via `Finset.lcm`. This creates a contradiction: $n_k$ divides the LCM of strictly smaller moduli, but the partition property requires $n_k$ to contribute 'new' residue class structure.

title: Ordinary Covering Systems Exist
content: **covering_systems_exist**: Axiomatizes that ordinary covering systems (allowing overlaps) with distinct moduli all $> 1$ do exist. This contrasts with the impossibility of exact coverings: relaxing the partition requirement to mere coverage makes the problem solvable. Erdős's example $\{0 \pmod{2}, 0 \pmod{3}, 1 \pmod{4}, 5 \pmod{6}, 7 \pmod{12}\}$ is one such system.

title: Verified Exact Covering with Repeated Moduli
content: **exactCoveringWithRepeats**: A fully *verified* construction of an exact covering: $\{0 \pmod{2}, 1 \pmod{2}\}$ partitions $\mathbb{Z}$ into even and odd integers. All four structure fields are proved: `nonempty` and `positive_moduli` by `simp`, `covers` by case split on $x \bmod 2$ using `omega`. This demonstrates that the distinct-moduli constraint is essential for the impossibility — exact coverings exist when repeated moduli are allowed.
mathContext: $\{0 \pmod{2}, 1 \pmod{2}\}$ is a verified exact covering of $\mathbb{Z}$
